name: Carolus Magnus
pdTranslations: None. Charlemagne (c. 747-814) was a political and military figure; he left no significant Latin theological or philosophical corpus in Patrologia Latina suitable for translation.
modernTranslations: None.
untranslatedHighlights: All works (primarily capitularies, letters, decrees)

name: Auctor incertus (Hugo de S. Victore?)
pdTranslations: Uncertain attribution—requires work-level triage. If attributable to Hugo of St. Victor, his Didascalicon and other works exist in English translation (Jerome Taylor).
modernTranslations: Uncertain; Hugo of St. Victor: The Didascalicon (Taylor), if confirmed.
untranslatedHighlights: Entire entry needs per-work identification and verification before translation status can be determined.

name: Petrus Cellensis
pdTranslations: None identified in public-domain early collections (NPNF, ANF, CCEL).
modernTranslations: The Letters of Peter of Celle (Oxford Medieval Texts, trans. Julian Haseldine, 2001); Peter of Celle: Selected Works (Cistercian Publications, trans. Hugh Feiss, 1987). Good coverage of major works.
untranslatedHighlights: Some sermons and treatises remain untranslated; 177 epistles, 95 sermons, 4 treatises total—not all rendered in modern English yet.

name: Auctor incertus (Rufinus Aquileiensis?)
pdTranslations: Uncertain attribution—requires work-level triage. If attributable to Rufinus of Aquileia, Church History exists in English translation.
modernTranslations: Uncertain; Rufinus of Aquileia: The Church History, Books 10-11 (trans. Philip R. Amidon), if confirmed.
untranslatedHighlights: Entire entry needs per-work identification before translation status can be assessed.

name: Fulgentius Ruspensis
pdTranslations: None identified in NPNF/ANF/CCEL.
modernTranslations: Fulgentius: Selected Works (Fathers of the Church, vol. 95, trans. Robert B. Eno, 1997); Fulgentius of Ruspe: Correspondence on Christology and Grace (Fathers of the Church, vol. 126, trans. Donald Fairbairn & Rob Roy McGregor, 2013). Includes On the Truth of Predestination and Grace.
untranslatedHighlights: Substantial portions of the corpus (14 works total) remain untranslated; major early medieval theological writings not fully available in English.

name: Anastasius bibliothecarius
pdTranslations: Portions of conciliar translations (Seventh and Eighth Ecumenical Council Acts, 787 & 869-70) may appear in NPNF or other patristic collections as secondary material.
modernTranslations: Limited. Anastasius's primary corpus consists of translations from Greek (council acts, saints' legends), not original theological works. His Chronographia tripartita (compilation from Theophanes, Nicephorus, Syncellus) may be indirectly available through those sources.
untranslatedHighlights: Original works and compositions remain largely inaccessible in English; acts of ecumenical councils translated primarily for their doctrinal content, not Anastasius's authorship.

name: Odo Cluniacensis
pdTranslations: St. Odo of Cluny (biography by John of Salerno, trans. G. Sitwell, 1958)—about his life, not his works.
modernTranslations: The Occupatio (epic poem on Redemption) translated by Christopher A. Jones with modern English translation and detailed commentary (Brepols). Sitwell's biography of Odo by John of Salerno (1958).
untranslatedHighlights: Commentary on Gregory I's Moralia, Collationes (three books of moral essays), sermons, hymns, antiphons—most works remain untranslated; only biography and one epic poem available.

name: Guillelmus Tyrensis
pdTranslations: Medieval Middle English translation: William Caxton's 'Eracles' (1481), a condensed version of the Old French translation of William's History of Deeds Done Beyond the Sea.
modernTranslations: Dana Cushing's revised Middle English text with facing-page modern English translation of the Eracles. The Latin original exists in scholarly editions but full modern English translation of William's complete Latin History not comprehensively available.
untranslatedHighlights: William of Tyre's complete Latin chronicle of the Kingdom of Jerusalem—major parts lack modern scholarly English translation despite historical importance.

name: Sigebertus Gemblacensis
pdTranslations: None identified in NPNF/ANF/CCEL.
modernTranslations: Only draft excerpts from the Chronica sive chronographia universalis available (relating to Emperor Henry IV and Pope Gregory VII); full universal chronicle (c. 381-1111) lacks comprehensive English translation.
untranslatedHighlights: Entire Chronicon ab anno 381 ad 1113 (one of the most influential medieval universal chronicles)—no complete modern English translation found.

name: Willelmus Malmesburiensis
pdTranslations: John Sharpe's translation of Chronicle of the Kings of England (seminal 19th-c. translation) and Historia Novella.
modernTranslations: Gesta regum Anglorum (History of the English Kings, volumes 1-2, Oxford Medieval Texts, trans. R. A. B. Mynors, R. M. Thomson, M. Winterbottom); Gesta pontificum Anglorum (History of the English Bishops, Oxford Medieval Texts, trans. Michael Winterbottom & Rodney Malcolm Thomson); facing-page Latin/English editions for detailed commentary. Delphi Classics editions.
untranslatedHighlights: Most major works translated in modern scholarly editions; some minor works or specific passages may remain untranslated.

name: Flodoardus Remensis
pdTranslations: None identified in NPNF/ANF/CCEL.
modernTranslations: The Annals of Flodoard of Reims, 919-966 (trans. Bernard S. Bachrach & Steven Fanning, Broadview Press/University of Toronto Press, 2004, Readings in Medieval Civilizations and Cultures series). Historia Remensis ecclesiae remains untranslated.
untranslatedHighlights: Historia Remensis ecclesiae (History of the Church of Reims) and other chronicling work remain untranslated; Annals (919-966) is the only major work rendered in English.

name: Gregorius Turonensis
pdTranslations: History of the Franks may appear in NPNF or other 19th-c. patristic collections; public-domain translations available.
modernTranslations: Life of the Fathers (Translated Texts for Historians, vol. 1, trans. Edward James, TTH); History of the Franks (multiple modern editions including Penguin Classics); Glory of the Martyrs and Glory of the Confessors also translated. Comprehensive coverage of Gregory's major works.
untranslatedHighlights: Most major historical and hagiographical works translated; minor works or specific selections may remain untranslated.

name: Zacharias Chrysopolitanus
pdTranslations: None identified.
modernTranslations: None found. His Gospel harmony (Unum ex Quattuor sive De Concordia Evangelistarum) with grammatical and etymological commentary on Greek, Hebrew, and Latin words remains in Latin only.
untranslatedHighlights: Entire corpus of biblical commentaries (1 work, 241,691 words) lacks English translation. His commentary drawing on Ambrose, Augustine, and Jerome has no modern English rendering.

name: Guillelmus abbas
pdTranslations: Unknown. The specific identity of this 'Guillelmus abbas' (1268) cannot be definitively established from available sources.
modernTranslations: Unknown. Could potentially be William of Saint-Thierry (1075/80-1148) or William of Newburgh (1136-1201), both of whom have partial translations available, but the 1268 date does not align. Requires manuscript-level verification.
untranslatedHighlights: Cannot assess without definitive identification of author.

name: Eugyppius Africae
pdTranslations: None identified in NPNF/ANF/CCEL for Eugippius's original works.
modernTranslations: The Life of St. Severinus (1914 translation, online at tertullian.org). His Thesaurus Augustinianeus (selection of Augustine's writings) survives only as a historical compilation, not a translated work of his own theology.
untranslatedHighlights: Original theological works remain untranslated; Life of St. Severinus is the only English text available. Three works total—two remain inaccessible in English.

name: Joannes Cassianus
pdTranslations: Conferences and Institutes likely in NPNF or early anthologies; public-domain versions available.
modernTranslations: The Conferences (Ancient Christian Writers 57, trans. Boniface Ramsey, OP, 1997); The Institutes of the Cenobia (ACW 58, trans. Boniface Ramsey, OP, 2000). Earlier translation: The Conferences (trans. Colm Luibhéid, Paulist Press, 1985). Comprehensive scholarly coverage of all major works.
untranslatedHighlights: None—both major works extensively translated and annotated in modern scholarly editions.

name: Aelredus Rievallensis
pdTranslations: None identified in NPNF/ANF/CCEL.
modernTranslations: Spiritual Friendship (Cistercian Studies series, ed. Marsha L. Dutton); The Historical Works (trans. Jane Patricia Freeland, Dutton ed., includes Genealogy of Kings of the English, Life of Saint Edward, Battle of the Standard); Treatises and Pastoral Prayer (Cistercian Fathers Series, vol. 2, trans. David Knowles); De Institutione Inclusarum (various Cistercian translations); Homilies on the Prophetic Burdens of Isaiah (trans. Lewis White, Cistercian Fathers series). Extensive Cistercian Publications coverage.
untranslatedHighlights: Most of Aelred's 11 surviving works have been translated in Cistercian series; minor works or specific treatises may remain untranslated.

name: Helinandus Frigidi Montis
pdTranslations: None identified in NPNF/ANF/CCEL.
modernTranslations: The Verses on Death (Les Vers de la Mort) translated by Jenny Lind Porter with verse translation and commentary (Cistercian Publications, 1999). Chronicon (forty-nine books, c. 1211-1223) remains untranslated.
untranslatedHighlights: Chronicon (world chronicle, only partial manuscript survival) entirely untranslated. Five works total—only French poem translated; Latin chronicles remain inaccessible.

name: Primasius Adrumetanensis
pdTranslations: None identified in NPNF/ANF/CCEL.
modernTranslations: Commentary on Revelation—in progress for English translation by Library of Early Christian Sources as of December 2021; expected publication 2-3 years from that date. Status as of July 2026 unknown.
untranslatedHighlights: Commentary on Revelation remains untranslated (or possibly in press). One of only three major Apocalypse commentaries (3rd-8th centuries) without English translation. Three works total—status unknown for other two.

name: Petrus Cantor
pdTranslations: None identified in NPNF/ANF/CCEL.
modernTranslations: The Abel Distinctions (partial translation mentioned in sources; full translation status unclear). Summarized in scholarly literature but comprehensive modern English translation not readily available.
untranslatedHighlights: Substantial theological works on sacraments, canon law, and moral theology remain untranslated. Two major works total—translation coverage minimal.
